record.narrative: All new estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive signed values support and negative signed values oppose the claimed association. The PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency association remains the most robust newly supported dataset signal. It is positive and interval-excluding-zero in batch_a (H111, +0.234, 95% CI +0.125 to +0.342; R109), in the dominant Avana library (H112, +0.288, 95% CI +0.232 to +0.343; R110), and in STK11-loss cells (H113, +0.258, 95% CI +0.134 to +0.382; R111). H113 is scientifically interesting because STK11-loss is a relevant co-mutation context and the PTEN-loss exposed cell count is only 50, but the effect size and lower bound are still meaningful. I accept H111, H112, and H113 as dataset associations, and request independent validation only for H113 because it has the smallest exposed cell among these accepted PTEN/STAT3 contexts and is the most useful remaining robustness check. H114 confirms that KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 is robust in STK11-loss cells (+0.775, 95% CI +0.727 to +0.823; R112). H115 confirms TP53-intact/USP7 in STK11-loss cells (+0.490, 95% CI +0.312 to +0.667; R113). H116 confirms SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 in TP53-loss cells (+0.773, 95% CI +0.729 to +0.817; R114). These effects are enormous relative to the dependency-score scale, interval-excluding-zero, and do not require additional validation. The new mechanism probe H110 shows no meaningful association between KEAP1 loss and STAT3 dependency (+0.016, 95% CI -0.012 to +0.044; R108), so it is rejected. H25, H30, H73, and H77 are all small or interval-crossing and are rejected: KRAS mutation in STK11-intact cells does not show meaningful dependency_KRAS association; MYC amplification does not show dependency_POLR2A association; PIK3CA mutation does not meaningfully modify TP53-intact/USP7; and research marker E does not show WRN association. H98 cannot be assessed because the PTEN-loss by SMAD4-loss comparison has only 19 exposed cases, violating the cell-size rule; it remains unresolved and deferred as underpowered rather than rejected. Independent validation is requested for H113 because it is a newly accepted context-specific PTEN/STAT3 result with the greatest remaining uncertainty, while validation capacity remains limited.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

The currently best-supported dataset associations remain MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53-intact status with stronger USP7 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker or less-negative NFE2L2 dependency, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. I register a small set of targeted refinements and one new biologically motivated predictor. First, KEAP1 loss is tested as a new main predictor of dependency_STAT3 because NRF2-pathway activation and STAT3 signaling have plausible inflammatory and oxidative-stress cross-talk; the falsifiable prediction is that KEAP1-loss cells have more negative STAT3 dependency scores, with alternatives being no association or the opposite. Second, because PTEN loss is now the strongest newly validated association, I register three direct context checks: PTEN/STAT3 in batch_a, in the dominant Avana library, and in STK11-loss cells. These distinguish whether the PTEN/STAT3 association is robust across assay conditions and metabolic/co-mutation contexts, or is partly context-specific. Third, I test the accepted SMARCA4/SMARCA2 association in TP53-loss cells, the accepted TP53-intact/USP7 association in STK11-loss cells, and the accepted KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association in STK11-loss cells. record.narrative: All newly returned estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so a positive signed estimate supports the registered claim and a negative signed estimate opposes it. The PTEN-loss/dependency_STAT3 association is again strongly supported: in SMAD4-intact cells, H117 gives +0.259 (95% CI +0.205 to +0.313; R121), and in adherent growth-pattern cells, H123 gives +0.262 (95% CI +0.203 to +0.321; R127). These are meaningful on the dependency-score scale, interval-excluding-zero, and consistent with the already validated overall PTEN/STAT3 result and several context-specific accepted subgroup results. I accept both as dataset-supported context robustness checks and close them. The MSI-high/WRN association persists in TP53-intact cells: H122 gives +0.780 (95% CI +0.747 to +0.813; R126), an enormous effect relative to the dependency scale, so I accept and close H122. KEAP1-loss/dependency_NFE2L2 is similarly robust: H42 in TP53-intact cells gives +0.792 (95% CI +0.770 to +0.815; R128), and H43 in TP53-loss cells gives +0.810 (95% CI +0.763 to +0.857; R129). Both are far larger than practical relevance thresholds and interval-excluding-zero; I accept them. TP53-intact/dependency_USP7 is also supported separately in KRAS-mutant and KRAS-wild-type cells: H40 gives +0.410 (95% CI +0.260 to +0.561; R131), and H41 gives +0.392 (95% CI +0.311 to +0.473; R132). These are substantial effects and close out the KRAS context checks. The new formal interaction H118, testing whether the PTEN-loss/STAT3 effect is attenuated in TP53-loss cells, has a positive point estimate +0.097 but a 95% interval that crosses zero (-0.024 to +0.217; R122). This is not sufficient to accept modification, but because the point estimate is near the lower boundary of practical relevance and the interval includes moderate positive values, I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than rejecting it as exactly null. The two new p53-pathway probes for MDM2 and RPL11 do not support the registered hypotheses. H34, overall CDKN2A loss with dependency_MDM2 direction +1, gives a negative signed effect -0.117 (95% CI -0.152 to -0.082; R130), meaning the raw association is opposite the registered positive hypothesis and interval-excluding-zero. H119, the same predictor restricted to TP53-intact cells, also gives a negative signed effect -0.119 (95% CI -0.158 to -0.079; R123). Thus the registered CDKN2A-loss/MDM2-positive hypotheses are rejected. The data do point consistently toward the opposite sign, but because that reversal was not the registered claim, I treat it as post hoc hypothesis generation rather than an accepted claim. The MYC/RPL11 probes are null: H120 gives -0.009 (95% CI -0.034 to +0.015; R124), and the TP53-loss interaction H121 gives +0.016 (95% CI -0.038 to +0.069; R125); both interval-crossing and negligible in size. I do not request independent validation this iteration because the newly accepted findings corroborate already accepted and mostly already validated main associations, while the CDKN2A/MDM2 reversal is a post-hoc sign change that should be registered explicitly before being accepted or validated. These remain associations in this supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable claims.

Iteration 11/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are currently due, but I reassess several unresolved secondary claims as rejected to concentrate later analyses on the strongest and most actionable results. Those rejected claims include tiny or imprecise associations/interactions involving KRAS mutation, BRAF V600E, research marker D, ARID1A co-loss interaction, batch interactions, and MSI-high effects on DHX9 or WRN effects on BRCA2. All are either close to zero or have intervals crossing zero, and the observed magnitudes are not compelling relative to the 10% clinical-significance scale. I propose eight new comparisons. First, I test the new CDKN2A-loss/dependency_MDM2 reversal in TP53-loss cells and formally test whether it is attenuated in TP53-loss relative to TP53-intact cells; the interaction is coded with positive raw interaction indicating a stronger effect in the TP53-intact complement. I also test the CDKN2A reversal in batch_a as a technical robustness check. Second, I test MYC amplification as a new predictor of dependency_MDM2 and test whether any MYC effect is p53-dependent. Third, I test PTEN-loss/dependency_STAT3 in inflammatory and hypoxic contexts and formally test modification by STK11 loss. For interaction estimates, the returned signed values are already aligned with the registered direction: positive signed values support the registered interaction contrast, and negative signed values oppose it. I will regard interval-excluding-zero effects exceeding about 10% of the relevant outcome scale as meaningful, with effects near or above 0.1 dependency-score units being clearly substantial. Validation remains reserved for the CDKN2A/MDM2 reversal if the next appraise stage supports it.

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive signed values support a stronger dependency direction when the registered direction is -1 and support the registered interaction contrast when the registered contrast is interaction. The two due validations are decisive. H113 tests PTEN loss versus no PTEN loss within STK11-loss cells for dependency_STAT3. Discovery gave signed +0.258, 95% CI +0.134 to +0.382, and independent validation gave +0.339, adjusted CI +0.122 to +0.557. The validated lower bound exceeds the practical 0.1-dependency-score-unit benchmark used here, and the interval excludes zero with a large point estimate. I therefore accept H113 and close it. This strengthens the PTEN-loss dependency_STAT3 association beyond the main population, TP53-loss cells, and the smaller KY library, showing that it remains strong in Avana-library STK11-loss cells. H124 tests the newly reversed CDKN2A-loss association with dependency_MDM2 in the overall eligible population. Discovery gave signed +0.117, 95% CI +0.082 to +0.152, meaning CDKN2A-loss cells have more-negative dependency_MDM2 scores, i.e. stronger MDM2 dependency. Independent validation gave +0.132, adjusted CI +0.080 to +0.184. The lower bound is slightly below the practical 0.1 threshold, but the replicated point estimate exceeds it, the adjusted interval excludes zero, and the effect is consistent with TP53-intact, TP53-loss, and batch_a strata. I therefore accept H124 and close it as a moderate but replicated dataset association. With these validations, the dataset-supported main associations are now: MSI-high is associated with much stronger dependency_WRN; SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger dependency_SMARCA2; TP53-intact status is associated with stronger dependency_USP7; KEAP1 loss is associated with less-negative and therefore weaker dependency_NFE2L2; PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3; and CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger dependency_MDM2. The PTEN/STAT3 association is particularly well supported overall and in multiple contexts, including TP53-loss, KY-library, Avana-library STK11-loss, TP53-intact, adenocarcinoma, KEAP1-loss, batch_a, Avana, SMAD4-intact, adherent-growth, elevated IFN-gamma, and elevated hypoxia settings, although the formal TP53 interaction remains uncertain. The CDKN2A/MDM2 association is now supported overall and in TP53-intact, TP53-loss, and batch_a strata, with no evidence that TP53 loss modifies it. Important negative and scope-limiting findings remain: KRAS mutation does not show a meaningful association with dependency_KRAS in tested settings; BRAF V600E does not show a meaningful association with dependency_BRAF or dependency_KRAS; EGFR amplification does not show a meaningful dependency_EGFR association in tested settings; ERBB2 amplification does not show a meaningful dependency_ERBB2 association; MYC amplification is not associated with dependency_MDM2 or with dependency_RPL11, POLR2A, DHX9, KIF18A, or TMED10 in tested settings; SMAD4 loss is not associated with dependency_STAT3 overall; KEAP1 loss is not associated with dependency_STAT3 overall; PTEN loss is not associated with dependency_USP7, MDM2, or EGFR in tested settings; and the constructed research markers D/E/F are generally null. Unresolved uncertainty is mostly secondary or powered: H118, the formal PTEN/STAT3 interaction by TP53 loss, has a positive point estimate of +0.097 but an interval crossing zero, so it remains deferred; H98 cannot be assessed because of insufficient cell counts. The most informative next analyses are to ask whether accepted effects are context-dependent rather than merely robust. I registered interaction tests for IFN-gamma and hypoxia as modifiers of PTEN loss dependency_STAT3, and a test of MYC amplification as a modifier of CDKN2A loss dependency_MDM2. If these remain near null, the accepted effects should be treated as stable across measured contexts; if one is positive and precise, it would identify a biologically interesting context amplification. These conclusions remain associations in the supplied lung-cancer CRISPR dependency dataset and are not causal claims or automatic generalizations to other platforms or cohorts.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, so I use this explore stage to add one new predictor-outcome comparison and eight focused effect-modifier tests for already accepted dataset associations. MYC amplification versus no MYC amplification is tested against dependency_SMARCA2 with an uncertain expectation because SMARCA2 has a wide dynamic range and chromatin or replication programs could plausibly interact with MYC, but prior MYC amplification probes were null for several dependencies. For the accepted main associations, I test whether they remain stable across genomic, proliferative, plasticity, or signaling contexts: mutation burden and aneuploidy for MSI-high dependency_WRN, proliferation and stemness for SMARCA4 loss dependency_SMARCA2, high MYC expression for KEAP1 loss dependency_NFE2L2, high EMT for PTEN loss dependency_STAT3, proliferation for CDKN2A loss dependency_MDM2, and aneuploidy for TP53-intact dependency_USP7. Direction coding: for mean_difference or interaction claims with direction -1, positive signed evidence corresponds to lower dependency scores, i.e. stronger dependency; direction +1 corresponds to higher scores, i.e. weaker dependency. For interactions, positive signed evidence supports a stronger or same-direction effect inside the listed high-context subgroup relative to its complement, while negative signed evidence supports attenuation or opposite modification; values near zero support stability. These thresholds were chosen to balance cells where possible, especially using mutation burden near the median rather than a more extreme quartile threshold. Active registered modifier tests H134, H135, and H136 remain relevant and are not duplicated. All conclusions sought here are dataset associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

H145 tests whether high aneuploidy modifies the TP53-intact-versus-TP53-loss effect on dependency_USP7. Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction

Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not

Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
All new estimates are already signed to the registered direction, so positive signed values support the registered contrast or amplification inside the specified subgroup relative to its complement. The strongest new result is H134: PTEN loss has a stronger association with dependency_STAT3 in high IFN-gamma signature contexts than in the complement, signed interaction +0.221, 95% CI +0.104 to +0.338 (R144). The point estimate is large relative to the overall PTEN/STAT3 main effect and the lower bound exceeds the conservative practical relevance marker I have used for these dependency-score contrasts. Therefore I accept H134 as dataset-supported evidence of IFN-gamma context amplification, but I keep it active because this is an interaction discovered in a setting with many exploratory comparisons and independent validation capacity is now exhausted. I registered lower-threshold and higher-threshold IFN sensitivity tests to judge robustness.

Most other modifier tests are null or too small. H135 (hypoxia modifying PTEN/STAT3) is essentially null, H136 (MYC amplification modifying CDKN2A/MDM2) is null, H137 (MYC amplification predicting dependency_SMARCA2) is null, H139/H140/H141 (aneuploidy, proliferation, or stemness modifying WRN or SMARCA2 associations) are near zero and interval crossing zero, H142 (MYC expression modifying KEAP1/NFE2L2) is null, H144 (proliferation modifying CDKN2A/MDM2) is null, and H145 (aneuploidy modifying TP53-intact/USP7) is null. I reject and close these because they provide no evidence of meaningful context dependence under the tested thresholds.

H138 cannot be evaluated because the high mutation burden threshold leaves zero exposed cells in the interaction complement, giving diagnostic insufficient_cell_n. This is an analytic specification problem, not evidence of absence, so I leave the claim scientifically unresolved but close the specified test. H143, PTEN/STAT3 modified by high EMT score, is positive (+0.141, CI +0.011 to +0.271; R153), but the interval lower bound is very close to zero, the exposed high-EMT cell is small, and the threshold is top-quartile. Given multiplicity and possible sensitivity to threshold, I keep H143 unresolved and active pending broader median-threshold and pre-specified 0.5-threshold sensitivity analyses. No validation request is possible because remaining new validation requests are zero. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

Iteration 12/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

  "narrative": "No new validation was released and no claims are currently due for reassessment, so this synthesis updates the scientific conclusion based on the evidence already in the ledger. The strongest conclusion is that the supplied lung-cancer CRISPR dependency dataset contains a compact set of scientifically meaningful associations, most of which have been independently replicated. MSI-high cells show much stronger dependency_WRN than microsatellite-stable cells (signed discovery estimate +0.790; independent validation +0.771). SMARCA4 loss shows much stronger dependency_SMARCA2 (discovery +0.784; validation +0.807), a pattern compatible with known paralog/paralog-like dependency structure but still interpreted here as a dataset association rather than a proven causal mechanism. TP53-intact cells have stronger dependency_USP7 than TP53-loss cells (TP53-intact minus TP53-loss, signed +0.396; validation +0.435). KEAP1 loss is associated with less-negative dependency_NFE2L2 scores, meaning weaker apparent NFE2L2 dependency, rather than stronger dependency (signed +0.796; validation +0.781). PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3 (signed +0.267; validation +0.274). CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger dependency_MDM2 after sign reversal of the initial expectation (signed +0.117; independent validation +0.132). These effects are far larger than the practical threshold used in this project and have consistent discovery and validation point estimates. For the CRISPR dependency-score contrasts, I interpret roughly 0.1 dependency-score-unit differences as scientifically/practically meaningful, using the project's clinical-significance emphasis as a guide but not asserting clinical relevance for CRISPR scores. The only caveat is that the adjusted validation lower bound for CDKN2A loss and dependency_MDM2 is slightly below 0.1, although the validated point estimate exceeds it and the finding is replicated.

The PTEN-loss association with dependency_STAT3 is especially robust. It is supported in the main population and in multiple strata, including TP53-intact and TP53-loss cells, adenocarcinoma cells, the two major CRISPR libraries, STK11-loss cells, KEAP1-loss cells, batch_a cells, adherent-growth cells, elevated IFN-gamma signature cells, and elevated hypoxia-score cells. The main population interaction H134 adds that this association is stronger in high IFN-gamma signature contexts than in the complement (signed interaction +0.221; 95% CI +0.104 to +0.338). I accept H134 as dataset-supported evidence of context amplification, but keep it active for threshold-sensitivity analyses because no independent validation capacity remains and interaction testing carries multiplicity risk. The CDKN2A-loss association with dependency_MDM2 is also robust overall and in TP53-intact, TP53-loss, and batch_a strata, and existing interaction tests do not show modification by TP53 loss, MYC amplification, or proliferation.

Important negative findings are scientifically informative. Canonical genotype-outcome contrasts were repeatedly null: KRAS mutation does not show a meaningful association with dependency_KRAS, BRAF V600E does not show a meaningful association with dependency_BRAF or dependency_KRAS, EGFR amplification does not show a meaningful association with dependency_EGFR, and ERBB2 amplification does not show a meaningful association with dependency_ERBB2. MYC amplification is null for dependency_RPL11, POLR2A, DHX9, KIF18A, TMED10, MDM2, and SMARCA2 in the tested comparisons. record.narrative:
No new validation was released and no claims are currently due for reassessment, so this synthesis updates the scientific conclusion based on the evidence already in the ledger. The strongest conclusion is that the supplied lung-cancer CRISPR dependency dataset contains a compact set of scientifically meaningful associations, most of which have been independently replicated. MSI-high cells show much stronger dependency_WRN than microsatellite-stable cells (signed discovery estimate +0.790; independent validation +0.771). SMARCA4 loss shows much stronger dependency_SMARCA2 (discovery +0.784; validation +0.807), a pattern compatible with known paralog/paralog-like dependency structure but still interpreted here as a dataset association rather than a proven causal mechanism. TP53-intact cells have stronger dependency_USP7 than TP53-loss cells (TP53-intact minus TP53-loss, signed +0.396; validation +0.435). KEAP1 loss is associated with less-negative dependency_NFE2L2 scores, meaning weaker apparent NFE2L2 dependency, rather than stronger dependency (signed +0.796; validation +0.781). PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3 (signed +0.267; validation +0.274). CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger dependency_MDM2 after sign reversal of the initial expectation (signed +0.117; independent validation +0.132). These effects are far larger than the practical threshold used in this project and have consistent discovery and validation point estimates. For the CRISPR dependency-score contrasts, I interpret roughly 0.1 dependency-score-unit differences as scientifically/practically meaningful, using the project's clinical-significance emphasis as a guide but not asserting clinical relevance for CRISPR scores. The only caveat is that the adjusted validation lower bound for CDKN2A loss and dependency_MDM2 is slightly below 0.1, although the validated point estimate exceeds it and the finding is replicated.

The PTEN-loss association with dependency_STAT3 is especially robust. It is supported in the main population and in multiple strata, including TP53-intact and TP53-loss cells, adenocarcinoma cells, the two major CRISPR libraries, STK11-loss cells, KEAP1-loss cells, batch_a cells, adherent-growth cells, elevated IFN-gamma signature cells, and elevated hypoxia-score cells. The main population interaction H134 adds that this association is stronger in high IFN-gamma signature contexts than in the complement (signed interaction +0.221; 95% CI +0.104 to +0.338). I accept H134 as dataset-supported evidence of context amplification, but keep it active for threshold-sensitivity analyses because no independent validation capacity remains and interaction testing carries multiplicity risk. The CDKN2A-loss association with dependency_MDM2 is also robust overall and in TP53-intact, TP53-loss, and batch_a strata, and existing interaction tests do not show modification by TP53 loss, MYC amplification, or proliferation.

Important negative findings are scientifically informative. Canonical genotype-outcome contrasts were repeatedly null: KRAS mutation does not show a meaningful association with dependency_KRAS, BRAF V600E does not show a meaningful association with dependency_BRAF or dependency_KRAS, EGFR amplification does not show a meaningful association with dependency_EGFR, and ERBB2 amplification does not show a meaningful association with dependency_ERBB2. MYC amplification is null for dependency_RPL11, POLR2A, DHX9, KIF18A, TMED10, MDM2, and SMARCA2 in the tested comparisons. PTEN loss is not associated with dependency_USP7, dependency_MDM2, or dependency_EGFR in the tested settings. The constructed research markers D, E, and F are generally null across the outcomes tested, which helps establish that these arbitrary assays are not driving the accepted results.

Unresolved uncertainty is now mostly focused on secondary context dependence and analytic power. H118, the formal PTEN/STAT3 interaction by TP53 loss, has a positive point estimate of +0.097 with an interval crossing zero, so it remains uncertain and deferred. H98 and H138 are unassessable as specified because the chosen thresholds leave insufficient cells in an interaction cell; this is an analytic specification issue, not evidence of absence. H143, PTEN/STAT3 modified by EMT score above the top quartile, is positive but borderline (+0.141; 95% CI +0.011 to +0.271), and I keep it unresolved and active pending broader-threshold sensitivity analyses. H146 and H147, which test lower- and higher-threshold IFN-gamma sensitivity for the PTEN/STAT3 interaction, and H148/H149 for EMT sensitivity, have not yet returned evidence. Because no voluntary validation requests remain, the next most informative analyses are to execute these registered sensitivity analyses and, if possible, retest the MSI-high WRN context using an alternative mutation-burden threshold that satisfies the minimum-cell constraint. All conclusions are associations in this supplied dataset; they do not establish causality and do not guarantee generalization to other CRISPR platforms, cohorts, or biological contexts.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due, so this explore stage adds eight scientifically motivated comparisons. H146-H149 remain active and are the registered threshold-sensitivity tests for the accepted PTEN/STAT3 IFN-gamma amplification and the borderline EMT result; if analysis capacity is limited, those should still be considered together with these new claims. Validation capacity is exhausted, so these proposals are all discovery-stage dataset comparisons, not causal or generalizable tests.

The first proposal refines the failed H138. H138 failed because the interaction cell required MSI-high cells below mutation burden 5 and there were none. Instead, I request the direct MSI-high versus MSS mean difference for dependency_WRN within mutation_burden >= 5. With direction -1, positive signed evidence means MSI-high cells have more negative dependency_WRN scores, i.e. stronger WRN dependency, within high-burden tumors.

The next proposals test plausible modifiers of already accepted associations. For dependency_USP7, I test whether the TP53-intact-versus-TP53-loss contrast is modified by PTEN loss. For dependency_NFE2L2, I test whether PIK3CA-mutant contexts amplify the KEAP1-loss-associated less-negative, weaker-dependency direction; with direction +1, positive signed evidence supports that hypothesis. For dependency_MDM2, I test whether MTAP loss modifies the accepted CDKN2A-loss association, relevant because MTAP often co-occurs with CDKN2A loss but is mechanistically distinct.

For dependency_SMARCA2, I test whether ARID1A loss has an additional association within SMARCA4-loss cells. The previous interaction test did not establish modification, but the direct co-loss contrast remains scientifically useful because SWI/SNF component losses can be context dependent. I also request a ploidy-high interaction for the SMARCA4-loss association, since chromosomal instability may modify chromatin/replication dependencies.

I add two broader exploratory claims. One tests whether TP53 loss alone predicts dependency_WRN, given p53 pathway effects on replication stress and DNA damage response. The other tests whether PTEN-loss association with dependency_STAT3 varies with high serum/culture-condition context using media_serum_pct >= 9; this is a robustness and culture-context test with likely sufficient cells. For all interaction claims, positive signed estimates indicate amplification of the registered contrast inside the listed context relative to its complement; interval-crossing or near-zero estimates indicate stability or absence of meaningful modification. I regard roughly 0.1 dependency-score-unit effects as practically meaningful for these contrasts, using the supplied clinical-significance emphasis as a guide rather than asserting clinical clinical relevance.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No assessments are due. I use the 12-test analysis budget to obtain new discovery evidence on the 12 active, previously registered claims that currently have no returned evidence: H146-H149 are threshold-sensitivity interactions for the accepted IFN-gamma context amplification and borderline EMT modification of PTEN loss on dependency_STAT3. H150 tests the MSI-high effect on dependency_WRN within high mutation-burden contexts, avoiding the cell-count failure of the prior H138 interaction specification. H151-H157 follow up accepted dependencies with biologically motivated modifiers or additional contrasts: PTEN loss as a modifier of TP53-intact dependency_USP7, PIK3CA mutation as a modifier of KEAP1-loss dependency_NFE2L2, MTAP loss as a modifier of CDKN2A-loss dependency_MDM2, direct ARID1A-loss effect within SMARCA4 loss, TP53-loss main effect on dependency_WRN, high-serum context modification of PTEN-loss dependency_STAT3, and high ploidy modification of SMARCA4-loss dependency_SMARCA2. I do not select already tested claims because they reuse existing evidence and provide no new sample. All estimates will be interpreted as signed to the registered direction; positive values support the registered contrast or context amplification relative to the complement, while interval-crossing or near-zero values support stability or absence of meaningful modification. These remain dataset associations, not causal claims.

Iteration 13/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset, not causal or externally generalizable claims.","synthesize":"No new validation was released and no claims are currently due for reassessment, so this synthesis updates the scientific conclusion based on the evidence already in the ledger. The strongest conclusion is that the supplied lung-cancer CRISPR dependency dataset contains a compact set of scientifically meaningful associations, most of which have been independently replicated. MSI-high cells show much stronger dependency_WRN than microsatellite-stable cells (signed discovery estimate +0.790; independent validation +0.771). SMARCA4 loss shows much stronger dependency_SMARCA2 (discovery +0.784; validation +0.807), a pattern compatible with known paralog/paralog-like dependency structure but still interpreted here as a dataset association rather than a proven causal mechanism. TP53-intact cells have stronger dependency_USP7 than TP53-loss cells (TP53-intact minus TP53-loss, signed +0.396; validation +0.435). KEAP1 loss is associated with less-negative dependency_NFE2L2 scores, meaning weaker apparent NFE2L2 dependency, rather than stronger dependency (signed +0.796; validation +0.781). PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3 (signed +0.267; validation +0.274). CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger dependency_MDM2 after sign reversal of the initial expectation (signed +0.117; independent validation +0.132). These effects are far larger than the practical threshold used in this project and have consistent discovery and validation point estimates. For the CRISPR dependency-score contrasts, I interpret roughly 0.1 dependency-score-unit differences as scientifically/practically meaningful, using the project's clinical-significance emphasis as a guide but not asserting clinical relevance for CRISPR scores. The only caveat is that the adjusted validation lower bound for CDKN2A loss and dependency_MDM2 is slightly below 0.1, although the validated point estimate exceeds it and the finding is replicated.\n\nThe PTEN-loss association with dependency_STAT3 is especially robust. It is supported in the main population and in multiple strata, including TP53-intact and TP53-loss cells, adenocarcinoma cells, the two major CRISPR libraries, STK11-loss cells, KEAP1-loss cells, batch_a cells, adherent-growth cells, elevated IFN-gamma signature cells, and elevated hypoxia-score cells. The main population interaction H134 adds that this association is stronger in high IFN-gamma signature contexts than in the complement (signed interaction +0.221; 95% CI +0.104 to +0.338). I accept H134 as dataset-supported evidence of context amplification, but keep it active for threshold-sensitivity analyses because no independent validation capacity remains and interaction testing carries multiplicity risk. The CDKN2A-loss association with dependency_MDM2 is also robust overall and in TP53-intact, TP53-loss, and batch_a strata, and existing interaction tests do not show modification by TP53 loss, MYC amplification, or proliferation.\n\nImportant negative findings are scientifically informative.
