Until such evidence, all conclusions should remain dataset-specific associations."}}

record.narrative: Final synthesis: No new validation estimates arrived and independent validation requests are exhausted, and assessments_due was empty. The final interpretation is descriptive and dataset-specific: these are measured associations among predictors and CRISPR dependency scores in the supplied 2000-cell lung adenocarcinoma-heavy dataset, not causal claims and not guaranteed generalizable claims. Because many overlapping subgroup tests were performed, I used a conservative practical benchmark of about 0.1 absolute dependency-score units and accepted direct strata only when the signed estimate and lower confidence limit were clearly above that threshold, while validated main effects were allowed to certify the central comparison. Supported findings: MSI-high cells have much stronger WRN dependency, H8/R8 estimate 0.790, 95 percent interval 0.760 to 0.819, independently validated by R39 estimate 0.771, 0.720 to 0.822; this effect also persists in screen_nnmd strata, R270 estimate 0.791 with lower bound 0.747 and R271 estimate 0.788 with lower bound 0.748, and in strict screen and Cas9 QC strata, R254 estimate 0.802 and R266 estimate 0.824. SMARCA4-loss cells have much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, H9/R9 estimate 0.784, 0.765 to 0.803, validated by R26 estimate 0.807, 0.777 to 0.838; the association persists in both ARID1A co-loss and ARID1A-intact strata, with smaller but validated ARID1A co-loss subset R66 estimate 0.820, and is robust across screen_nnmd strata, R272 lower bound 0.734 and R273 lower bound 0.779. TP53-intact cells have stronger USP7 dependency than TP53-loss cells, H12/R12 estimate 0.396, 0.325 to 0.467, validated by R40 estimate 0.435, 0.334 to 0.536; this persists in KRAS-mutant and KRAS wild-type contexts, R131 lower bound 0.260 and R132 lower bound 0.311, and across screen_nnmd strata, R274 lower bound 0.259 and R275 lower bound 0.324, with a smaller but validated Ky library estimate R53 lower bound 0.129. KEAP1-loss cells have weaker apparent NFE2L2 dependency, interpreted as less negative dependency scores, H13/R7 estimate 0.796, 0.776 to 0.816, validated by R13 estimate 0.781, 0.752 to 0.809; it remains large across screen_nnmd strata, R276 estimate 0.793 lower bound 0.764 and R277 estimate 0.799 lower bound 0.771. PTEN-loss cells have stronger STAT3 dependency, H85/R73 estimate 0.267, 0.215 to 0.319, validated by R79 estimate 0.274, 0.200 to 0.348; this is the broadest accepted context association, with many accepted direct strata across TP53, KRAS, lineage, growth pattern, mutation burden, aneuploidy, IFN-gamma, hypoxia, EMT, screen quality, Cas9 activity, and screen_nnmd, for example R138, R169, R262, R263, R252, R264, R278 lower bound 0.247 and R279 lower bound 0.139. CDKN2A-loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency, accepted as H124/R130 estimate 0.117, 0.082 to 0.152 and validated by R143 estimate 0.132, 0.080 to 0.184, though this is the smallest accepted effect and the earlier opposite-direction H34 remains rejected. Context stability: the four largest core effects are robust to technical screen-quality and Cas9-activity splits, and the new screen_nnmd direct strata support stability for WRN, SMARCA2, USP7, NFE2L2, and STAT3. However, stability of direct strata does not certify a general interaction model. Many interaction tests were imprecise or null, including H226 screen-quality interaction for STAT3/PTEN rejected by R241, H224 high-screen IFN interaction unresolved with R239 crossing zero, and most WRN, SMARCA2, USP7, and NFE2L2 interactions rejected. CDKN2A/MDM2 screen_nnmd strata remain unresolved because R280 lower bound 0.060 and R281 lower bound 0.075 fall below the practical benchmark. Negative findings: canonical driver concordance is absent or negligible in this dataset, KRAS mutation does not predict dependency_KRAS, R1 estimate 0.014, BRAF V600E does not predict dependency_BRAF, R3 estimate -0.017, EGFR amplification does not predict dependency_EGFR, R5 estimate 0.025, and ERBB2 amplification does not predict dependency_ERBB2, R6 estimate 0.001. TP53 loss alone is not a practical predictor of MDM2, STAT3, WRN, or RPL11 dependency, R11, R100, R165, R90. MYC amplification is essentially null across RPL11, POLR2A, KIF18A, TMED10, DHX9, MDM2, SMARCA2, and WRN, with small estimates and intervals that are either null or far below the practical benchmark; WRN R231 estimate -0.033 is directionally weak. ARID1A loss is not a practical independent SMARCA2 marker, R86 estimate -0.017, and ARID1A inside SMARCA4-loss cells is also not practical, R164 estimate 0.034. MTAP loss is not a robust independent predictor: it does not predict MDM2 among CDKN2A-intact cells, R258 estimate 0.004, and it does not predict STAT3 or USP7 main effects, R260 and R261; MTAP effect inside CDKN2A-loss cells is also not practical, R253 estimate 0.064. PTEN specificity is supported because PTEN loss is not practical for USP7, MDM2, or WRN, R103, R104, R173. Other tested genomic, clinical, technical, and research-marker variables largely behaved as null or below practical thresholds, including research markers D, E, and F. Unresolved uncertainty: the CDKN2A MDM2 main effect is validated, but attribution to MTAP co-loss versus MTAP-intact cells remains uncertain; direct CDKN2A subset estimates are compatible in magnitude but have lower bounds below the practical rule, including R248 estimate 0.165 lower 0.081 and R249 estimate 0.105 lower 0.067. Strict technical QC subsets for CDKN2A are sometimes unresolved, such as R259 estimate 0.147 lower 0.060, or rejected, such as R265 estimate 0.037 crossing zero. The screen_nnmd interaction structure is unresolved because H276 through H281 have no evidence and are now closed as unresolved; H224 high-screen IFN interaction is unresolved. Some direct low-boundary strata, such as H170, remain unresolved under the conservative rule despite point estimates above 0.1. Generalizability and causality remain uncertain because predictors co-occur, QC eligibility can induce selection, some cells are near minimum sample size, and repeated subgroup probing increases multiplicity risk. Most informative next analysis: external held-out replication of the six core associations, WRN/MSI, SMARCA2/SMARCA4, USP7/TP53-intact, NFE2L2/KEAP1, STAT3/PTEN, and MDM2/CDKN2A, using pre-specified effect thresholds and multiplicity control. If only same-dataset work is possible, multivariable or cross-validated models adjusting for co-occurring genomic events are more informative than further one-way subgroup strata; the priority same-dataset questions are CDKN2A subset attribution with MTAP and TP53 co-status, IFN-gamma interaction structure for PTEN/STAT3, and whether technical screen-quality variables modify the core effects in interaction rather than direct-stratum analyses.

Iteration 24/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: Independent validation is exhausted and no claim assessments are due, so the remaining exploration should focus on resolving the most important unresolved interaction and attribution questions rather than accumulating more one-way accepted strata. First, for PTEN-loss and dependency_STAT3, the main effect and many direct strata are accepted, but the IFN-gamma interaction structure remains incomplete: full-population IFN>=0.5 and low-screen IFN>=0.5 interaction evidence are supportive, high-screen IFN>=0.5 is unresolved, and IFN>=0 interactions are weaker. I therefore propose a high-screen IFN>=0 interaction. Under direction -1, a positive signed estimate means the PTEN-loss STAT3-dependency effect is more negative, i.e. stronger, in IFN-positive high-screen cells than in IFN-negative high-screen cells. If this clears about 0.1 absolute dependency-score units, it would suggest a broader IFN-related effect modification in high-quality screens; if not, the IFN interaction may remain restricted to lower screen-quality or higher IFN-threshold contexts. Second, the validated MDM2 effect associated with CDKN2A loss is the smallest accepted core effect and its attribution to CDKN2A versus co-occurring MTAP loss remains uncertain. I propose direct CDKN2A effects in TP53-intact MTAP-intact and TP53-intact MTAP-loss cells, a direct MTAP effect within CDKN2A-loss TP53-intact cells, and an interaction between CDKN2A and MTAP within TP53-intact cells. For the direct CDKN2A claims, direction -1 means a positive signed estimate supports stronger MDM2 dependency in CDKN2A-loss cells. For the MTAP direct claim, direction -1 means positive supports stronger MDM2 dependency with MTAP loss, but the expected direction is uncertain. For the CDKN2A-by-MTAP interaction, direction +1 means positive signed evidence corresponds to a raw interaction in which the CDKN2A effect is less negative, or more attenuated, among MTAP-loss cells relative to MTAP-intact cells. This pattern would support MTAP co-loss or pathway interaction as an important confounder or modifier; an interaction near zero would support CDKN2A as the primary measured predictor in TP53-intact cells. Third, although accepted core effects are generally robust in direct screen-quality strata, effect modification by high Cas9 activity remains less fully characterized. I add interactions at cas9_activity_pct>=85 for STAT3/PTEN, MDM2/CDKN2A, and USP7/TP53-intact. For these direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates mean stronger dependency-score contrasts in high-Cas9 cells than in lower-Cas9 cells. Large positive interactions would indicate technical Cas9 dependence; null or small interactions would support context stability, while strong negative interactions would suggest stronger effects in lower-Cas9 cells. These are all dataset-specific association hypotheses, not causal or generalizability claims. Because many overlapping subgroup tests have been performed, I will continue to use about 0.1 absolute dependency-score units as a conservative practical benchmark, accepting only estimates whose signed lower confidence bound clearly exceeds that threshold for the relevant direction, rejecting small or null-crossing effects, and leaving compatible but sub-threshold estimates unresolved.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

prompt:
Iteration 24/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: No independent validation was requested because remaining voluntary validation requests are exhausted. All newly delivered estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction and were interpreted without re-signing. Audit first: every reported comparison has adequate Welch cell counts, no diagnostic invalidity, and no apparent leakage beyond measured predictors in the supplied dataset. The main threat to these interaction/attribution claims is multiplicity, co-occurrence of genomic and technical variables, and the fact that many subgroup tests are overlapping and not independent. Using the pre-specified conservative practical benchmark of about 0.1 absolute dependency-score units with lower confidence bounds clearly beyond that bound, the new evidence mostly fails to certify practical effect modification, while a few CDKN2A/MTAP subset estimates remain directionally compatible but imprecise. H282 tests PTEN-loss effect modification by IFN-gamma positivity within high screen_roc_auc cells for dependency_STAT3. R282 signed estimate is +0.0357 with interval -0.1103 to +0.1817. Because direction is -1, a positive estimate would mean the PTEN-loss STAT3 contrast is stronger in IFN-positive high-screen cells than in IFN-negative high-screen cells. The estimate is small and crosses zero, but the interval is wide enough that meaningful practical modification is not excluded in either direction; therefore H282 is unresolved and closed as a final same-dataset probe. This does not overturn accepted lower-screen or higher-threshold IFN-gamma interactions, but it does not support a broad practical IFN-gamma interaction restricted to high screen quality. H283 and H284 test CDKN2A-loss effects on dependency_MDM2 within TP53-intact cells stratified by MTAP status. R283 gives +0.1064 with lower bound 0.0631 in TP53-intact MTAP-intact cells, and R284 gives +0.1624 with lower bound 0.0701 in TP53-intact MTAP-loss cells. Both use direction -1, so positive signed estimates mean CDKN2A-loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency. The point estimates are compatible with the validated CDKN2A main effect, but neither lower bound exceeds the conservative 0.1 benchmark, especially with the small MTAP-loss exposed cell count. Thus both remain unresolved rather than accepted as independent practical strata. H285 tests whether MTAP loss adds a direct dependency_MDM2 association within CDKN2A-loss TP53-intact cells. R285 is +0.0648 with interval -0.0340 to +0.1635. The estimate is small, crosses zero, and does not meet the practical lower-bound rule; combined with earlier null or subthreshold MTAP claims, H285 is rejected as evidence for a practical independent MTAP effect in this CDKN2A-loss context. H286 tests whether MTAP co-loss attenuates the CDKN2A effect within TP53-intact cells using direction +1, so positive signed evidence would mean attenuation of the normally stronger CDKN2A dependency contrast among MTAP-loss cells. R286 is -0.0560 with interval -0.1576 to +0.0456. The signed estimate is opposite the registered attenuation hypothesis and the upper bound is far below the practical benchmark, so H286 is rejected as evidence for attenuation. The wide lower bound suggests the dataset cannot exclude small opposite-direction modification, but it does not support the planned practical interaction and should not be interpreted as establishing one. H287-H289 test high Cas9 activity effect modification for PTEN-loss STAT3, CDKN2A-loss MDM2, and TP53-intact USP7. All use direction -1, so positive signed estimates would indicate stronger contrast in high-Cas9 cells than in lower-Cas9 cells. R287 is -0.0381 [-0.1558, 0.0796], R288 is +0.0102 [-0.0682, 0.0886], and R289 is -0.0433 [-0.2010, 0.1145]. None provides practical support for high-Cas9 amplification; R287 and R288 have upper bounds below the benchmark and near-zero estimates, while R289 is small and zero-crossing. These are rejected as practical effect-modification claims, supporting descriptive stability of the corresponding accepted associations rather than technical Cas9 dependence. H276-H279 test screen_nnmd median-split interaction modification for WRN/MSI, SMARCA2/SMARCA4, USP7/TP53-intact, and NFE2L2/KEAP1. R290 is +0.0032 [-0.0562, 0.0626], R291 is -0.0463 [-0.0850, -0.0076], R292 is -0.0463 [-0.1904, 0.0978], and R293 is -0.0070 [-0.0473, 0.0334]. All are small, and none has a lower bound beyond the practical benchmark in the relevant direction. H277 excludes zero but the absolute magnitude is below the benchmark, so it is a small practical null. Therefore all four screen_nnmd interaction hypotheses are rejected as practical effect modification. This is consistent with the accepted direct screen_nnmd strata: the core associations are descriptively stable across screen_nnmd groups, while these interaction analyses do not show meaningful modification. Overall, these results do not change the accepted core dataset-specific associations: MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53-intact status with stronger USP7 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker apparent NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency. The new attribution probes make MTAP co-loss less likely as a practical independent driver of the MDM2 effect, but CDKN2A subset attribution remains unresolved because direct TP53-intact MTAP strata are compatible in magnitude yet underpowered at the strict lower-bound threshold. All conclusions remain associations in this supplied dataset and do not establish causality or generalizability.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
Final synthesis: No new validation results arrived at this stage, assessments_due is empty, and the independent validation budget is exhausted. All cited estimates are already signed to the registered claim direction and are interpreted without further re-signing. Given continuous dependency scores that can be negative, the stated 10 percent relative threshold was operationalized conservatively as an approximate 0.1 absolute dependency-unit lower-bound practical benchmark, with validated main effects accepted when supported by independent replication even when smaller direct-stratum estimates remained below that threshold. The conclusions below are descriptive associations in the supplied 2000-cell lung, adenocarcinoma-heavy dataset, not causal statements and not generalization guarantees.

Supported core findings. First, MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency: H8/R8 estimate 0.790, 95 percent interval 0.760 to 0.819, independently validated by R39 estimate 0.771, interval 0.720 to 0.822. It persists across technical strata, including screen_nnmd splits R270 and R271 and strict screen-quality or Cas9 strata R254 and R266, and across many genomic subgroups. Second, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency: H9/R9 estimate 0.784, interval 0.765 to 0.803, validated by R26 estimate 0.807, interval 0.777 to 0.838. This holds in ARID1A-intact cells R75 and ARID1A co-loss cells R65, with the ARID1A co-loss subset validated by R66, and is descriptively stable across screen_nnmd strata R272 and R273 and strict QC strata R255 and R267. Third, TP53-intact status is associated with stronger USP7 dependency than TP53 loss: H12/R12 estimate 0.396, interval 0.325 to 0.467, validated by R40 estimate 0.435, interval 0.334 to 0.536. It persists in KRAS-mutant R131 and KRAS wild-type R132 cells and across screen_nnmd strata R274 and R275 and strict QC strata R256 and R268; the smaller Ky-library stratum remains accepted and validated by R53. Fourth, KEAP1 loss is associated with higher, less negative, apparent NFE2L2 dependency scores, meaning weaker apparent dependency: H13/R7 estimate 0.796, interval 0.776 to 0.816, validated by R13 estimate 0.781, interval 0.752 to 0.809; this also remains large across screen_nnmd strata R276 and R277 and strict QC strata R257 and R269. Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H85/R73 estimate 0.267, interval 0.215 to 0.319, validated by R79 estimate 0.274, interval 0.200 to 0.348. This is the broadest accepted context association, with many accepted direct strata across TP53, KRAS, lineage, growth pattern, mutation burden, aneuploidy, IFN-gamma, hypoxia, EMT, screen quality, Cas9 activity, and screen_nnmd, for example R138, R169, R220, R262, R263, R252, R264, R278, and R279. Sixth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: H124/R130 estimate 0.117, interval 0.082 to 0.152, validated by R143 estimate 0.132, interval 0.080 to 0.184. This is the smallest accepted core effect and is not fully attributed to co-occurring MTAP status.

Context and specificity. Several negative findings clarify specificity. Canonical driver concordance is absent: KRAS mutation does not predict dependency_KRAS in a practical direction, R1 estimate 0.014 with interval -0.004 to 0.031; BRAF V600E does not predict dependency_BRAF, R3 estimate -0.017, interval -0.045 to 0.012; EGFR amplification does not predict dependency_EGFR, R5 estimate 0.025, interval -0.000 to 0.051; ERBB2 amplification does not predict dependency_ERBB2, R6 estimate 0.001, interval -0.027 to 0.030. TP53 loss alone is not a practical predictor of MDM2 R11, STAT3 R100, WRN R165, or RPL11 R90. MYC amplification is null or below practical thresholds across RPL11 R21, POLR2A R116, KIF18A R78, TMED10 R45, DHX9 R64, MDM2 R136, SMARCA2 R147, and WRN R235, where R235 is a small opposite-direction estimate. ARID1A loss is not a practical independent SMARCA2 marker, R86, and is not practical within SMARCA4-loss cells, R164. PTEN specificity is supported because PTEN loss is not practical for USP7 R103, MDM2 R104, or WRN R173. MTAP loss is not a robust independent predictor: MTAP main effects are small or null for MDM2 R176, STAT3 R260, and USP7 R261; MTAP within CDKN2A-loss TP53-intact cells is not practical R285; and the MTAP attenuation interaction for CDKN2A is not supported R286. Research markers D, E, and F behaved as null or practically insignificant assay controls, for example R15, R17, R142, R24, R25, R35, R118, and R141.

Unresolved uncertainty. The strongest residual uncertainty is attribution of the validated CDKN2A-MDM2 association. Direct subset estimates are directionally compatible but do not clear the conservative lower-bound benchmark: TP53-intact CDKN2A estimates include R123 lower 0.079, R283 lower 0.063, and R284 lower 0.070; MTAP stratified estimates include R248 lower 0.081 and R249 lower 0.067; strict technical subsets can be subthreshold or null, for example R259 lower 0.060 and R265 crossing zero. These do not overturn the validated main effect but prevent acceptance of MTAP co-loss as a practical independent driver or modifier, while small modification cannot be fully excluded. IFN-gamma interaction structure for PTEN loss and STAT3 dependency remains incomplete: accepted IFN-gamma interactions include R144 for IFN-gamma at least 0.5, R157 for IFN-gamma at least 0.66, and the lower-screen interaction R225, but high-screen interactions R239 and R282 remain zero-crossing and unresolved. Other unresolved issues include some lower-bound direct strata such as R179 and some CDKN2A screen_nnmd strata R280 and R281. Interaction tests for WRN, SMARCA2, USP7, and NFE2L2 mostly failed to show practical modification, and screen_nnmd interactions R290 through R293 were rejected as practical effects. Some claims lacked valid cells, such as R119 and R148, and were not used as evidence.

Overall conclusion and next analysis. The evidence supports six dataset-specific associations: MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53-intact status with stronger USP7 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker apparent NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency. The first four are very large and robust across many splits within this dataset; STAT3/PTEN is moderately large and broad; MDM2/CDKN2A is validated but smaller and attributionally uncertain. The most informative next analysis is external held-out replication of these six core associations using pre-specified thresholds and multiplicity control. If restricted to this dataset, the best follow-up is joint multivariable or cross-validated models adjusting for co-occurring genomic events, with pre-specified interactions, rather than more one-way subgroup strata. Priority same-dataset questions are CDKN2A versus MTAP and TP53 attribution for MDM2, IFN-gamma interaction structure for PTEN and STAT3, and whether screen quality or Cas9 activity modify core effects in formal interaction models.

Iteration 25/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

For the MTAP direct claim, direction -1 means positive supports stronger MDM2 dependency with MTAP loss, but the expected direction is uncertain. For these direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates mean stronger dependency-score contrasts in high-Cas9 cells than in lower-Cas9 cells. The point estimates are compatible with the validated CDKN2A main effect, but neither lower bound exceeds the conservative 0.1 benchmark, especially with the small MTAP-loss exposed cell count. Thus both remain unresolved rather than accepted as independent practical strata. H285 tests whether MTAP loss adds a direct dependency_MDM2 association within CDKN2A-loss TP53-intact cells. R285 is +0.0648 with interval -0.0340 to +0.1635. The estimate is small, crosses zero, and does not meet the practical lower-bound rule; combined with earlier null or subthreshold MTAP claims, H285 is rejected as evidence for a practical independent MTAP effect in this CDKN2A-loss context. H286 tests whether MTAP co-loss attenuates the CDKN2A effect within TP53-intact cells using direction +1, so positive signed evidence would mean attenuation of the normally stronger CDKN2A dependency contrast among MTAP-loss cells. R286 is -0.0560 with interval -0.1576 to +0.0456. The signed estimate is opposite the registered attenuation hypothesis and the upper bound is far below the practical benchmark, so H286 is rejected as evidence for attenuation. The wide lower bound suggests the dataset cannot exclude small opposite-direction modification, but it does not support the planned practical interaction and should not be interpreted as establishing one. H287-H289 test high Cas9 activity effect modification for PTEN-loss STAT3, CDKN2A-loss MDM2, and TP53-intact USP7. All use direction -1, so positive signed estimates would indicate stronger contrast in high-Cas9 cells than in lower-Cas9 cells. R287 is -0.0381 [-0.1558, 0.0796], R288 is +0.0102 [-0.0682, 0.0886], and R289 is -0.0433 [-0.2010, 0.1145]. These are rejected as practical effect-modification claims, supporting descriptive stability of the corresponding accepted associations rather than technical Cas9 dependence. H276-H279 test screen_nnmd median-split interaction modification for WRN/MSI, SMARCA2/SMARCA4, USP7/TP53-intact, and NFE2L2/KEAP1. R290 is +0.0032 [-0.0562, 0.0626], R291 is -0.0463 [-0.0850, -0.0076], R292 is -0.0463 [-0.1904, 0.0978], and R293 is -0.0070 [-0.0473, 0.0334]. All are small, and none has a lower bound beyond the practical benchmark in the relevant direction. H277 excludes zero but the absolute magnitude is below the benchmark, so it is a small practical null. Therefore all four screen_nnmd interaction hypotheses are rejected as practical effect modification. This is consistent with the accepted direct screen_nnmd strata: the core associations are descriptively stable across screen_nnmd groups, while these interaction analyses do not show meaningful modification. All conclusions remain associations in this supplied dataset and do not establish causality or generalizability.","synthesize":"Final synthesis: No new validation results arrived at this stage, assessments_due is empty, and the independent validation budget is exhausted. All cited estimates are already signed to the registered claim direction and are interpreted without further re-signing. Given continuous dependency scores that can be negative, the stated 10 percent relative threshold was operationalized conservatively as an approximate 0.1 absolute dependency-unit lower-bound practical benchmark, with validated main effects accepted when supported by independent replication even when smaller direct-stratum estimates remained below that threshold. The conclusions below are descriptive associations in the supplied 2000-cell lung, adenocarcinoma-heavy dataset, not causal statements and not generalization guarantees.\\n\\nSupported core findings. First, MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency: H8/R8 estimate 0.790, 95 percent interval 0.760 to 0.819, independently validated by R39 estimate 0.771, interval 0.720 to 0.822. It persists across technical strata, including screen_nnmd splits R270 and R271 and strict screen-quality or Cas9 strata R254 and R266, and across many genomic subgroups. Second, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency: H9/R9 estimate 0.784, interval 0.765 to 0.803, validated by R26 estimate 0.807, interval 0.777 to 0.838. This holds in ARID1A-intact cells R75 and ARID1A co-loss cells R65, with the ARID1A co-loss subset validated by R66, and is descriptively stable across screen_nnmd strata R272 and R273 and strict QC strata R255 and R267. Third, TP53-intact status is associated with stronger USP7 dependency than TP53 loss: H12/R12 estimate 0.396, interval 0.325 to 0.467, validated by R40 estimate 0.435, interval 0.334 to 0.536. It persists in KRAS-mutant R131 and KRAS wild-type R132 cells and across screen_nnmd strata R274 and R275 and strict QC strata R256 and R268; the smaller Ky-library stratum remains accepted and validated by R53. Fourth, KEAP1 loss is associated with higher, less negative, apparent NFE2L2 dependency scores, meaning weaker apparent dependency: H13/R7 estimate 0.796, interval 0.776 to 0.816, validated by R13 estimate 0.781, interval 0.752 to 0.809; this also remains large across screen_nnmd strata R276 and R277 and strict QC strata R257 and R269. Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H85/R73 estimate 0.267, interval 0.215 to 0.319, validated by R79 estimate 0.274, interval 0.200 to 0.348. This is the broadest accepted context association, with many accepted direct strata across TP53, KRAS, lineage, growth pattern, mutation burden, aneuploidy, IFN-gamma, hypoxia, EMT, screen quality, Cas9 activity, and screen_nnmd, for example R138, R169, R220, R262, R263, R252, R264, R278, and R279. Sixth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: H124/R130 estimate 0.117, interval 0.082 to 0.152, validated by R143 estimate 0.132, interval 0.080 to 0.184. This is the smallest accepted core effect and is not fully attributed to co-occurring MTAP status.\\n\\nContext and specificity. Several negative findings clarify specificity. Canonical driver concordance is absent: KRAS mutation does not predict dependency_KRAS in a practical direction, R1 estimate 0.014 with interval -0.004 to 0.031; BRAF V600E does not predict dependency_BRAF, R3 estimate -0.017, interval -0.045 to 0.012; EGFR amplification does not predict dependency_EGFR, R5 estimate 0.025, interval -0.000 to 0.051; ERBB2 amplification does not predict dependency_ERBB2, R6 estimate 0.001, interval -0.027 to 0.030. TP53 loss alone is not a practical predictor of MDM2 R11, STAT3 R100, WRN R165, or RPL11 R90. MYC amplification is null or below practical thresholds across RPL11 R21, POLR2A R116, KIF18A R78, TMED10 R45, DHX9 R64, MDM2 R136, SMARCA2 R147, and WRN R235, where R235 is a small opposite-direction estimate. ARID1A loss is not a practical independent SMARCA2 marker, R86, and is not practical within SMARCA4-loss cells, R164. PTEN specificity is supported because PTEN loss is not practical for USP7 R103, MDM2 R104, or WRN R173. MTAP loss is not a robust independent predictor: MTAP main effects are small or null for MDM2 R176, STAT3 R260, and USP7 R261; MTAP within CDKN2A-loss TP53-intact cells is not practical R285; and the MTAP attenuation interaction for CDKN2A is not supported R286. Research markers D, E, and F behaved as null or practically insignificant assay controls, for example R15, R17, R142, R24, R25, R35, R118, and R141.\\n\\nUnresolved uncertainty. The strongest residual uncertainty is attribution of the validated CDKN2A-MDM2 association. Direct subset estimates are directionally compatible but do not clear the conservative lower-bound benchmark: TP53-intact CDKN2A estimates include R123 lower 0.079, R283 lower 0.063, and R284 lower 0.070; MTAP stratified estimates include R248 lower 0.081 and R249 lower 0.067; strict technical subsets can be subthreshold or null, for example R259 lower 0.060 and R265 crossing zero. These do not overturn the validated main effect but prevent acceptance of MTAP co-loss as a practical independent driver or modifier, while small modification cannot be fully excluded. IFN-gamma interaction structure for PTEN loss and STAT3 dependency remains incomplete: accepted IFN-gamma interactions include R144 for IFN-gamma at least 0.5, R157 for IFN-gamma at least 0.66, and the lower-screen interaction R225, but high-screen interactions R239 and R282 remain zero-crossing and unresolved. Other unresolved issues include some lower-bound direct strata such as R179 and some CDKN2A screen_nnmd strata R280 and R281. Interaction tests for WRN, SMARCA2, USP7, and NFE2L2 mostly failed to show practical modification, and screen_nnmd interactions R290 through R293 were rejected as practical effects. Some claims lacked valid cells, such as R119 and R148, and were not used as evidence.\\n\\nOverall conclusion and next analysis. The evidence supports six dataset-specific associations: MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53-intact status with stronger USP7 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker apparent NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency. The first four are very large and robust across many splits within this dataset; STAT3/PTEN is moderately large and broad; MDM2/CDKN2A is validated but smaller and attributionally uncertain. The most informative next analysis is external held-out replication of these six core associations using pre-specified thresholds and multiplicity control. If restricted to this dataset, the best follow-up is joint multivariable or cross-validated models adjusting for co-occurring genomic events, with pre-specified interactions, rather than more one-way subgroup strata. Priority same-dataset questions are CDKN2A versus MTAP and TP53 attribution for MDM2, IFN-gamma interaction structure for PTEN and STAT3, and whether screen quality or Cas9 activity modify core effects in formal interaction models."}}

record.narrative: At the final exploration stage, no scientifically useful new comparisons are registered. The independent validation budget is exhausted, no assessments are due, and the key same-dataset association, specificity, attribution, and technical-interaction probes have already been completed. The accepted core dataset-specific associations remain: MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency; SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency; TP53-intact status with stronger USP7 dependency; KEAP1 loss with weaker apparent NFE2L2 dependency; PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency; and CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency. Remaining unresolved issues are mostly attribution or interaction questions that cannot be resolved decisively with additional one-way subgroup tests in this dataset without adding multiplicity and instability. Further progress would require external held-out replication and pre-specified joint multivariable or cross-validated models with multiplicity control. Therefore, new exploratory comparisons in this supplied dataset are not expected to change the evidentiary interpretation.

prompt:
Iteration 25/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Audit first: every reported comparison has adequate Welch cell counts, no diagnostic invalidity, and no apparent leakage beyond measured predictors in the supplied dataset. The main threat to these interaction/attribution claims is multiplicity, co-occurrence of genomic and technical variables, and the fact that many subgroup tests are overlapping and not independent. Using the pre-specified conservative practical benchmark of about 0.1 absolute dependency-score units with lower confidence bounds clearly beyond that bound, the new evidence mostly fails to certify practical effect modification, while a few CDKN2A/MTAP subset estimates remain directionally compatible but imprecise. H282 tests PTEN-loss effect modification by IFN-gamma positivity within high screen_roc_auc cells for dependency_STAT3. R282 signed estimate is +0.0357 with interval -0.1103 to +0.1817. Because direction is -1, a positive estimate would mean the PTEN-loss STAT3 contrast is stronger in IFN-positive high-screen cells than in IFN-negative high-screen cells. The estimate is small and crosses zero, but the interval is wide enough that meaningful practical modification is not excluded in either direction; therefore H282 is unresolved and closed as a final same-dataset probe. This does not overturn accepted lower-screen or higher-threshold IFN-gamma interactions, but it does not support a broad practical IFN-gamma interaction restricted to high screen quality. H283 and H284 test CDKN2A-loss effects on dependency_MDM2 within TP53-intact cells stratified by MTAP status. R283 gives +0.1064 with lower bound 0.0631 in TP53-intact MTAP-intact cells, and R284 gives +0.1624 with lower bound 0.0701 in TP53-intact MTAP-loss cells. Both use direction -1, so positive signed estimates mean CDKN2A-loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency. The point estimates are compatible with the validated CDKN2A main effect, but neither lower bound exceeds the conservative 0.1 benchmark, especially with the small MTAP-loss exposed cell count. Thus both remain unresolved rather than accepted as independent practical strata. H285 tests whether MTAP loss adds a direct dependency_MDM2 association within CDKN2A-loss TP53-intact cells. R285 is +0.0648 with interval -0.0340 to +0.1635. The estimate is small, crosses zero, and does not meet the practical lower-bound rule; combined with earlier null or subthreshold MTAP claims, H285 is rejected as evidence for a practical independent MTAP effect in this CDKN2A-loss context. H286 tests whether MTAP co-loss attenuates the CDKN2A effect within TP53-intact cells using direction +1, so positive signed evidence would mean attenuation of the normally stronger CDKN2A dependency contrast among MTAP-loss cells. R286 is -0.0560 with interval -0.1576 to +0.0456. The signed estimate is opposite the registered attenuation hypothesis and the upper bound is far below the practical benchmark, so H286 is rejected as evidence for attenuation. The wide lower bound suggests the dataset cannot exclude small opposite-direction modification, but it does not support the planned practical interaction and should not be interpreted as establishing one. H287-H289 test high Cas9 activity effect modification for PTEN-loss STAT3, CDKN2A-loss MDM2, and TP53-intact USP7. All use direction -1, so positive signed estimates would indicate stronger contrast in high-Cas9 cells than in lower-Cas9 cells. R287 is -0.0381 [-0.1558, 0.0796], R288 is +0.0102 [-0.0682, 0.0886], and R289 is -0.0433 [-0.2010, 0.1145].
